items.title: Ant Colony Development Wiki
items.text:
Ant Colony is a small, finishable, single-player 2D side-view colony simulation built in Unity 6. The design centres on persistent individual ants, physical work, destructible terrain, and an authored-content-first development approach.

This wiki is a readable development companion to the repository's authoritative documents. It describes the confirmed design, the current implementation, and the evidence behind milestone status without treating planned work as finished gameplay.

Current accepted baseline

Milestone 3.2A: individual needs and survival foundation.

Latest implemented slice

Milestone 3.2B: physical food, water, and rest interactions — pending manual acceptance.

Engine

Unity 6000.3.8f1, 2D URP, C#, new Input System.

Status vocabulary

Planned means approved design or roadmap intent, not code. Implemented means the repository contains the feature. Automated tested means named tests were executed successfully. Accepted means the required manual Unity checks were also confirmed. These labels are not interchangeable.

items.title: Start here
items.text:
• Game Overview explains the vision, player role, and scope.
  • Gameplay Mechanics maps the main loops and their current status.
  • Ant Movement and Navigation covers the most mature technical gameplay foundation.
  • Technical Architecture shows ownership and data flow.
  • Development Roadmap identifies the next authorised action and future milestones.
  • Milestone History records implementation and validation evidence.
  • Design Decision Log summarises approved decisions and unresolved choices.

items.title: Sources of truth
items.text:
The wiki is derived from, but does not replace:

  1. Documentation/GameDesignDocument.md for approved design intent.
  2. Documentation/CurrentGameState.md for implemented and verified behavior.
  3. Documentation/DevelopmentRoadmap.md for milestone ordering, scope, and acceptance gates.
  4. The Unity assets, C# source, tests, and recorded results for repository reality.

If these disagree, contributors must report the discrepancy instead of silently choosing a version. See the documentation workflow.

items.title: Visual gallery
items.text:
Future screenshot: integrated development world, three selectable ants, functional Background tiles, and navigation diagnostics.

Place future images in docs/assets/screenshots/ and diagrams in docs/assets/diagrams/, then link them from the relevant system page.

items.title: Approved job model
items.text:
Future autonomous work uses a per-ant matrix of priorities 1–4 plus Disabled. The highest eligible priority wins before the closest reachable job by path cost. Skills change efficiency; they do not override player-assigned priority.

Ants may also receive temporary explicit orders. Critical survival may interrupt ordinary work at a safe point. Valid partial progress persists, and exclusive reservations prevent two ants from consuming or owning the same work target. Drafted survival intervention remains unresolved.

items.title: Current implementation
items.text:
The general job system is not implemented. Existing command behavior is deliberately narrower:

  • Ants can be selected individually.
  • Right-click issues Move, Eat, Drink, or Rest according to target context.
  • Orders have explicit travel, interaction, completion, cancellation, and failure states.
  • Movement uses the shared grid navigation service and motor.
  • 3.2B uses stable-ant reservations for physical resources and sleeping positions.
  • A valid order continues when the player changes selection.

These seams are useful foundations, but they do not establish colony-wide work discovery, autonomous survival, priority evaluation, or generic job ownership.

items.title: Future decision flow
items.text:
flowchart TD
  A[Ant available] --> S{Critical survival?}
  S -- Yes --> I[Interrupt safely and reserve survival job]
  S -- No --> O{Explicit order?}
  O -- Yes --> E[Validate and execute order]
  O -- No --> P[Find highest enabled work priority]
  P --> R[Filter eligible reachable unreserved jobs]
  R --> C[Choose lowest path cost]
  C --> X[Reserve, travel, work, and commit]
  I --> X
  E --> X
  X --> A

items.title: Required architecture boundaries
items.text:
• Job choice must not live in UI code.
  • Navigation calculates routes; it does not decide why an ant travels.
  • Work progress and physical resources remain authoritative outside visuals.
  • Cancellation and interruption must release reservations exactly once.
  • Construction preserves builder self-supply.
  • Hundreds-of-ants goals require controlled update rates and shared data, but do not justify DOTS/ECS before profiling.

items.title: Not implemented
items.text: Priority matrices, job categories, colony designations, work scanning, critical-survival autonomy, safe interruption thresholds, generic reservations, hauling, excavation, construction, Draft Mode, group tactics, local avoidance, and persistence all require separately approved milestones.

items.title: Ant Movement and Navigation
items.text: Movement and navigation are the most extensively implemented and tested foundations in the project. They deliberately separate world truth, movement capability, route planning, and motor execution.

items.title: Authoritative rules
items.text:
• Every resident coordinate has one Background Tile and at most one foreground Solid Tile.
  • A blocking Solid prevents occupancy; excavation will remove only eligible foreground material.
  • Exposed natural Earth and Stone Backgrounds are grippable at normal speed.
  • Prepared Background grants the same access with a provisional 1.25x movement-speed multiplier.
  • Sky is non-grippable; without ground or grip an ant can fall.
  • Full-body clearance is separate from grip, grounding, traversability, and reachability.
  • Valid diagonal connections cannot cut blocked corners.
  • Stable movement follows shared navigation; Rigidbody2D gravity is reserved for Falling.

items.title: Production flow
items.text:
flowchart LR
  W[ChunkedWorldData] --> C[Clearance and capability]
  W --> M[Shared GridNavigationMap]
  C --> M
  M --> P[GridPathfinder and scheduler]
  P --> S[GridNavigationWorldService]
  S --> G[GridNavigationMotor]
  G --> V[Ant visual and status]

GridNavigationWorldService is the per-world owner of the shared map and bounded scheduler. GridNavigationMotor exposes the narrow destination, cancellation, and status boundary used by selection and survival interactions. The command layer does not implement a competing movement system.

items.title: Known limitations
items.text:
• Friendly overlap is currently intentional; local avoidance and congestion behavior are future work.
  • The current grid is a deterministic authored development world, not procedural streaming gameplay.
  • General multiple-ant traffic, reservations, and deadlock handling are not complete gameplay systems.
  • The older AntSurfaceMotor and PlayerMovementInput course remains for regression testing. It is not the normal control model.
  • The original movement prototype still has pending ceiling, complete-corner-route, Auto Step-Over, and camera-follow completion work; that does not invalidate the accepted grid-navigation milestones.

items.title: Future acceptance
items.text:
Dynamic excavation and functional conversion must locally invalidate affected navigation data. Future agents must use the same route and motor rules; they cannot teleport, fly through unsupported space, or bypass clearance because a task system requested it.

Future diagram or screenshot: grid anchors, prepared-speed region, falling transition, and an invalidated route after terrain mutation.

items.title: Implemented identity model
items.text:
Each ant is represented by one authoritative plain-C# AntRecord. Stable AntId and ColonyId values, caste, attributes, lifecycle, skills, and needs belong to the record rather than to the visual GameObject. AntEntityBinding connects a runtime visual to an existing record, while a visual-claim registry prevents duplicate live representations.

The deterministic development ants are:

Name Caste Strength Agility Endurance Mara Queen 7 5 8 Pip Worker 4 8 5 Tala Worker 6 6 7

This identity and attribute foundation is complete and manually accepted. Visual destruction does not delete the record, and deceased records reject movement orders. Save/load and actual death gameplay are not implemented.

items.title: Implemented skill foundation
items.text:
Queen and Worker records share seven ordinary skills:

  • Excavation
  • Surface Preparation
  • Construction
  • Hauling
  • Foraging
  • Combat
  • Brood Care

All begin at level 0 and can reach level 100. A successful future activity can call the explicit learn-by-doing API; starting or cancelling work must not award experience.

items.title: Provisional progression
items.text:
• XP needed from level L to L+1: 100 + 5L.
  • Cumulative XP at level L: 100L + 2.5L(L-1).
  • Level 100 caps at 34,750 total XP.
  • After a provisional 24-hour inactivity grace period, skill value above 50 decays by 0.25 levels per inactive hour and stops at 50.
  • Needs and Rested modifiers can multiply a valid XP award without changing stored base progression rules.

These values are development placeholders. The foundation is implemented and automated-tested; its manual acceptance was recorded through the approved transition to milestone 3.2A.

items.title: Planned individuality
items.text: The approved design expects equipment, permanent death, work efficiency from skills, and persistent individual histories. Roles will affect autonomous priorities rather than lock ants out of normal skills. Exact attribute formulas, equipment effects, ageing, and save serialization remain unresolved or unimplemented.

items.title: Boundaries
items.text:
• Skills never silently outrank player-assigned work priorities.
  • The current work-speed multiplier is exposed for future jobs and does not alter navigation speed.
  • The temporary ordered-work productivity bonus is approved in principle, but its value and implementation remain TBD.
  • A working founding queen is the intended start; older ordinary-ant-to-queen progression language is superseded.

See Food, Water and Survival for needs modifiers and Ant AI and Job Management for future priority selection.

items.title: Brood and Reproduction
items.text: Brood and reproduction are approved design, not implemented gameplay.

items.title: Founding sequence
items.text:
The intended first controllable ant is a working founding queen. The early colony sequence is:

  1. Excavate an accessible chamber.
  2. Construct at least three Nursery Background tiles.
  3. Explicitly authorise an initial brood of three larvae.
  4. Physically feed the larvae on multiple occasions.
  5. Allow surviving brood to mature into three individually controllable general-purpose workers.

This supersedes older plans in which an ordinary player ant later transformed into a queen.

items.title: Approved rules
items.text:
• Reproduction always requires explicit player authorisation; spare capacity alone cannot trigger it.
  • Each functional Nursery Background tile supplies exactly one brood slot.
  • Nursery function can operate without an enclosing room.
  • Proper enclosure may grant room-quality efficiency, but not extra base capacity.
  • Removing occupied nursery capacity pauses development rather than silently deleting brood.
  • Brood Care is one of the seven universal learn-by-doing skills.
  • Individual ant death is permanent once death gameplay exists.

items.title: Open decisions
items.text:
• Exact egg-to-larva-to-pupa-to-adult presentation and timing.
  • Feeding thresholds, resource types, and failure consequences.
  • Brood mortality and reassignment when capacity is removed.
  • Later brood sizes and queen work/reproduction trade-offs.
  • Colony behavior after queen death.

items.title: Dependencies
items.text:
Brood implementation depends on accepted excavation, resource-backed construction, Nursery conversion, physical food logistics, autonomous jobs, lifecycle transitions, and persistence. Those dependencies are not yet complete, so brood must not be introduced as an isolated shortcut.

See Colony Construction and Rooms, Food, Water and Survival, and Ant AI and Job Management.

items.title: Approved construction model
items.text:
Construction is physical, location-based work. Functional colony tiles are created by converting exposed Background cells after required materials are gathered and consumed. Recipes and balance remain unapproved.

The ant performing construction must personally gather and deliver its own materials, including multiple trips. A separate hauler must not silently complete the builder's supply responsibility. Reservations prevent double allocation; cancelling construction leaves unused delivered or reserved materials physical and recoverable.

items.title: Functional Backgrounds
items.text:
Approved functions include:

  • Nursery
  • Sleeping
  • Food Storage
  • Water Storage
  • Material Storage
  • production functions still to be specified
  • burial

Each functional Background tile provides one unit of base capacity. Material Storage uses one tile per inventory slot and may later support optional filters. Function and locomotion remain separate properties: a functional tile can still be traversable and grippable.

Milestone 3.2B authors Food Storage, Water Storage, and Sleeping cells as deterministic development fixtures. They replace the function/material of existing Background cells, remain traversable at 1.0x speed, and expose exactly one slot each. This validates direct interactions, not general construction, conversion, or room gameplay.

items.title: Rooms and doors
items.text: The approved design allows mixed-use spaces. Enclosure is not required for base tile function, but an enclosed specialised room may earn quality or efficiency bonuses. Every opening into an enclosed room requires a door. Exact enclosure detection, door rules, scoring, mixed-use penalties, and quality formulas remain unresolved.

items.title: Status
items.text:
Capability Status Functional Background data seam Implemented for selected development functions Authored Food/Water/Sleeping fixtures Implemented; 3.2B manual acceptance pending Physical resource reservation seam Implemented narrowly for Eat/Drink Material Storage Approved design only Construction jobs and builder self-supply Approved design only Conversion progress and cancellation recovery Planned, not implemented Room enclosure, doors, and quality Planned, not implemented Future screenshot: functional Background overlays, room boundary, door openings, and quality diagnostics.

See Excavation and Terrain for layer semantics and Ant AI and Job Management for reservation and interruption rules.

items.title: Design Decision Log
items.text: This log summarises approved decisions. It does not approve unresolved details or replace the GDD.

items.title: Approved decisions
items.text: Date Decision Consequence 12 Oct 2026 Begin with a working founding queen Older ordinary-ant-to-queen start plans are superseded 12 Oct 2026 Use autonomous, temporary-order, and future Draft control states WASD movement remains a developer-only regression tool 12 Oct 2026 Share navigation and action mechanics between player orders and AI Command systems call existing services instead of creating parallel movement 12 Oct 2026 Natural Earth and Stone are intrinsically grippable Preparation improves speed rather than unlocking climbing 12 Oct 2026 Preserve permanent Background plus optional foreground Solid Excavation removes only eligible foreground material 12 Oct 2026 Make functional colony tiles resource-backed Background conversions Function, locomotion, and foreground occupancy stay separate 12 Oct 2026 Use one capacity unit per functional Background tile Nursery, storage, and sleeping capacity remain spatial and explicit 12 Oct 2026 Require a door at every opening of an enclosed room Room quality cannot assume open gaps are sealed 12 Oct 2026 Allow mixed-use rooms Specialisation may improve quality but does not invalidate base function 12 Oct 2026 Model resources and reservations physically Avoid unexplained global counters and duplicate consumption 12 Oct 2026 Make the builder self-supply construction Separate haulers do not fulfil the builder's material-gathering responsibility 12 Oct 2026 Use per-ant work priorities 1–4 plus Disabled Priority precedes path-cost choice; skills affect efficiency, not rank 12 Oct 2026 Preserve valid partial work across safe interruptions Critical needs can interrupt without erasing completed progress 12 Oct 2026 Require explicit brood authorisation Spare food or nursery capacity never triggers reproduction automatically 12 Oct 2026 Start the first brood at three larvae and three Nursery cells Early colony growth has a concrete spatial dependency 13 Oct 2026 Store identity, skills, and needs on authoritative ant records Visual replacement and selection changes do not transfer or erase ant state 13 Oct 2026 Keep 3.2B interactions narrow and location-owned No generic inventory, global stockpile, or autonomous job authority is implied

items.title: Open decisions
items.text:
• Exact ordered-work productivity bonus and eligible actions.
  • Job categories, interrupt thresholds, and explicit-order precedence.
  • Drafted-ant survival intervention.
  • Resource stack sizes, recipes, work durations, and final carrying balance.
  • Room enclosure algorithm, door behavior, and quality formulas.
  • Brood stages, timing, feeding thresholds, mortality, and overflow policy.
  • Queen-death colony outcome.
  • Combat, equipment, enemy behavior, and defence detail.
  • Save format, procedural generation rules, and chunk streaming lifecycle.
  • Final need rates, skill curve, decay, and interaction values.

items.title: Adding an entry
items.text: Record only decisions explicitly approved by the user or already marked authoritative in the GDD. Include the date, the decision, and its implementation consequence. If a topic is unresolved, add it to Open decisions instead of silently choosing a default.

items.title: Ordered future direction
items.text:
The numbered roadmap beyond the accepted foundation remains direction, not authorised implementation:

  1. Hybrid task assignment and colony-wide priorities.
  2. Multiple-ant movement, local avoidance, and congestion recovery.
  3. Autonomous worker and survival loops.
  4. Excavation, Surface Preparation, physical resources, and hauling.
  5. Functional construction, rooms, doors, and quality.
  6. Nursery, brood, reproduction, and colony growth.
  7. Population/performance scaling and persistence.
  8. Enemy colonies, equipment, combat, and defence.
  9. Finished-slice onboarding, objectives, save/load, and polish.

Detailed scope and acceptance criteria must be approved when each milestone begins. See Design Decision Log for unresolved dependencies.

items.title: Documentation Workflow
items.text: Documentation maintenance is part of milestone completion. It is not a separate optional cleanup task.

items.title: Source hierarchy
items.text:
1. Inspect code, authored Unity content, and actual test output.
  2. Update Documentation/CurrentGameState.md with what is implemented and verified.
  3. Update Documentation/DevelopmentRoadmap.md with status, evidence, and the next authorised action.
  4. Update Documentation/GameDesignDocument.md only when the user approves a design change.
  5. Synchronise the relevant pages in docs/.

If evidence conflicts, record the discrepancy. Do not convert a plan into an implementation claim or an automated result into manual acceptance.

items.title: Per-change checklist
items.text:
• Update the relevant system page in docs/.
  • Update Technical Architecture for ownership, data-flow, assembly, or scene-flow changes.
  • Add an entry to the Design Decision Log for a significant approved decision.
  • Update Development Roadmap and Milestone History when status or evidence changes.
  • Link related pages so readers can move between design, architecture, and milestone context.
  • Add screenshots or diagrams only when they show observed current behavior.
  • Run a clean strict Zensical build.
  • Report compilation, automated tests, and manual Unity acceptance separately.

items.title: Status language
items.text: Label Meaning Planned Approved or proposed intent; no implementation claim Implemented Relevant code/assets exist; validation may still be incomplete Automated tested Named test runs passed; not a claim about unobserved visuals or input Implemented — Pending Manual Acceptance Implementation and relevant automation exist, but required Unity checklist is still open Complete / Accepted All milestone acceptance evidence, including required manual checks, is confirmed Blocked A required check could not run; record the exact blocker rather than claiming success

items.title: Local preview
items.text:
From the Unity project root in PowerShell:

.\.venv-zensical\Scripts\zensical.exe serve

Open http://127.0.0.1:8000/. The server rebuilds the wiki when Markdown or configuration changes.

For the same validation used by CI:

.\.venv-zensical\Scripts\zensical.exe build --clean --strict

The generated site/ directory, .cache/, temporary setup files, and .venv-zensical/ are intentionally ignored by Git.

items.title: Images and diagrams
items.text:
• Store screenshots in docs/assets/screenshots/.
  • Store hand-authored diagram assets in docs/assets/diagrams/.
  • Prefer Mermaid for architecture flows that should remain text-reviewable.
  • Include concise alt text and identify the Unity scene and milestone shown.
  • Never use a future mock-up as evidence that a feature is implemented.

items.title: Two-layer world model
items.text:
The world foundation is implemented. Each cell in a resident 32×32 chunk contains exactly one permanent Background Material and zero or one foreground Solid Material. Missing chunks are unavailable rather than silently generated during a query.

The two layers have different responsibilities:

Layer Purpose Mutation rule Background Persistent substrate, grip, movement speed, and future colony function May be converted or prepared; never absent in a resident cell Foreground Solid Blocking/excavatable material and supporting geometry May be removed by future excavation when eligible

Visual Tilemaps and the collision-only Tilemap are projections of authoritative world data. The visual layers do not own gameplay state.

items.title: Implemented terrain foundations
items.text:
• Sparse signed-coordinate chunk data and explicit bounded generation.
  • Covered, Exposed, Supported, Unsupported, Unknown, and Unavailable classification.
  • Material definitions with independent movement-blocking and navigation-support flags.
  • Background and foreground Tilemap rendering.
  • A collision-only Tilemap with composite collider generation.
  • Whole-body rotated-capsule clearance queries.
  • Local refresh and navigation invalidation seams for controlled development mutations.
  • Natural Earth/Stone grip, Prepared speed, and non-grippable Sky behavior.

These systems are development foundations. They do not yet provide player-facing excavation work.

items.title: Approved excavation design
items.text:
The player will designate eligible foreground Solid cells for excavation. An assigned ant must reach a valid work position, make incremental progress, and remove only the foreground material when work completes. The Background remains. Excavated material becomes a physical resource: the excavator picks it up when slot capacity permits and otherwise drops it safely in the world.

Valid partial progress must survive safe interruptions. Dynamic terrain changes must refresh collision, movement capability, and relevant route data without rebuilding the entire world unconditionally.

items.title: Surface Preparation
items.text: Preparation is a future resource-backed Background conversion job. It does not unlock natural climbing: intact exposed Earth and Stone are already grippable. Prepared Background instead provides the provisional 1.25x travel-speed benefit. Exact recipes, work time, visual progression, and final balance are unresolved.

items.title: Not implemented
items.text:
• Excavation designations and worker selection.
  • Digging progress, completion, and physical soil creation.
  • Hauling or stockpile delivery.
  • Resource-backed preparation jobs.
  • Procedural generation, durable chunk streaming, or save/load.
  • Player-facing terrain tools outside deterministic development controls.

See Ant Movement and Navigation for mutation response and Colony Construction and Rooms for functional Background conversion.

items.title: Accepted needs foundation
items.text: Milestone 3.2A is complete and manually accepted. Every authoritative ant record owns Health, Hunger, Thirst, Fatigue, and Rested qualification. State persists through selection changes and visual rebinding, and a deterministic development-world rebuild resets it.

items.title: Provisional values
items.text:
Rule Development value Starting Health / Hunger / Thirst 100 / 100 / 100 Starting Fatigue 20 Awake Hunger loss 2 per simulation hour Awake Thirst loss 3 per simulation hour Awake Fatigue gain 4 per simulation hour Rest recovery 12 Fatigue per simulation hour Critical Hunger threshold 10 or lower Critical Hunger damage 2 Health per simulation hour Critical Thirst effect Blocks ordinary skill XP Rested qualification Completed rest at Fatigue 20 or lower Maximum Rested work speed 1.15x Maximum Rested skill XP 1.25x Rested fade Returns to 1.0x by Fatigue 80

The work multiplier is exposed for future jobs and does not alter navigation speed. Zero Health pauses ordinary survival advancement but does not yet create death or corpse gameplay.

items.title: Physical interactions
items.text:
Milestone 3.2B implements explicit player-issued Eat, Drink, and Rest interactions:

  • Food and water quantities belong to specific functional Background cells.
  • Resource and sleeping reservations belong to stable ant identities.
  • The ant chooses the lowest-cost reachable adjacent anchor through the shared grid pathfinder.
  • Arrival revalidates location and function before interaction.
  • Cancellation, replacement, failure, inactive/deceased state, and world reset release reservations.
  • Changing selection does not cancel another ant's valid order.

Eat reserves and consumes one resource.food.development unit after one simulation hour and restores 40 Hunger. Drink consumes one resource.water.development unit after one simulation hour and restores 50 Thirst. Rest recovers Fatigue over time and completes at the accepted Rested threshold. Interaction time advances at one simulation hour per real-time second in the development scene.

items.title: Not implemented
items.text:
Autonomous survival behavior, gathering, hauling, general inventories, cooking, food varieties, spoilage, water production, containers, permanent beds, colony-wide stock accounting, death, corpses, and save/load are outside the current slice.

See Development Roadmap before extending this system.

items.title: Vision
items.text:
Ant Colony is a single-player, scrollable and zoomable 2D side-view colony simulation. The intended world is procedural, persistent, chunk-loaded, and destructible. The player manages a colony at strategic scale while issuing explicit orders to persistent individual ants.

The game should remain small enough to finish. Depth comes from physical work, individual needs and skills, shared terrain rules, and colony logistics rather than from a large collection of disconnected systems.

items.title: Player fantasy
items.text: The player guides a founding queen and, later, a growing colony through excavation, survival, construction, brood care, and defence. Ants are individuals rather than anonymous counters: each retains identity, attributes, learned skills, health, hunger, thirst, fatigue, equipment, and lifecycle state as the relevant systems are implemented.

items.title: Intended core loop
items.text:
1. Explore and understand the local underground space.
  2. Excavate accessible foreground material without removing the permanent Background.
  3. Convert exposed Background cells into useful colony functions using physical resources.
  4. Secure food, water, sleeping capacity, and nursery capacity.
  5. Authorise brood and support it until new workers mature.
  6. Assign work through colony priorities or temporary explicit orders.
  7. Expand while maintaining individual survival and preparing for hostile encounters.

Only the foundations of this loop exist today. See Gameplay Mechanics for the system-by-system status.

items.title: Current playable development state
items.text:
The integrated AntGameDevelopment.unity scene is a deterministic development environment, not a finished game loop. It currently demonstrates:

  • authoritative two-layer world data and Tilemap projection;
  • whole-body clearance, Background grip, gravity, and grid navigation;
  • three selectable ants with persistent identity, attributes, skills, and needs;
  • independent movement orders through the production grid motor;
  • explicit physical Eat, Drink, and Rest interactions;
  • developer diagnostics and deterministic fixtures.

Milestone 3.2B is implemented and fully automated-tested, but its 20-step manual Play Mode checklist remains pending. Autonomous colony work, general inventories, construction, excavation gameplay, brood, room quality, combat, persistence, and a finished onboarding flow are not implemented.

items.title: Scope boundaries
items.text:
• Single-player only; no networking package is planned.
  • PC-first prototype.
  • The earlier continuous-input movement course remains a developer regression fixture, not the intended normal-play control scheme.
  • Numerical balance is provisional unless the GDD explicitly marks it approved.
  • Future ideas are not an implementation checklist and require a separately authorised milestone.

items.title: Control model
items.text:
The approved player-facing model has three states:

  • Autonomous: an ant selects work and survival behavior from allowed priorities when those systems exist.
  • Temporary explicit order: the player requests a specific task. Completion, cancellation, or invalidation returns the ant to autonomy.
  • Draft Mode: a future persistent tactical state for move, attack, hold, defend-area, retreat, and group control.

Current implementation supports selection plus temporary Move, Eat, Drink, and Rest orders. It does not yet implement the general autonomous job system or Draft Mode. The old WASD PlayerMovementInput path is retained strictly as a developer movement regression tool.

items.title: Physical-world principles
items.text:
• Terrain, resources, capacity, and work should exist at world locations rather than as unexplained global counters.
  • Ants must navigate to a valid adjacent interaction position before acting.
  • The constructing ant is responsible for gathering and delivering its own materials, including multiple trips.
  • Valid partial work survives safe interruptions.
  • Reservations prevent duplicate consumption and must be released on cancellation or failure.

The current 3.2B interaction slice proves those principles only for location-owned food, water, and sleeping reservations. It is not a generic inventory or job framework.

items.title: Progression and failure
items.text: Skills improve through successful work. Hunger, thirst, fatigue, and health create survival pressure. Individual ant death is intended to be permanent, but actual death and corpse gameplay are not implemented. The colony outcome after queen death remains unresolved.

items.title: 2.4A–2.4D — Production movement transition
items.text:
• 2.4A complete: natural Earth/Stone grip, Prepared 1.25x speed, and Sky falling; 56/56 focused Edit Mode, 227/227 full Edit Mode, 6/6 Play Mode, validators, and manual acceptance.
  • 2.4B complete: shared-map A* proof, smooth route following, falling/recovery, and recorded 1/100/300/500-agent benchmarks plus manual acceptance.
  • 2.4C complete: bounded fair scheduler, cancellation, terrain revisions, recovery, diagnostics, and successful deterministic request batches through 500 agents plus manual acceptance.
  • 2.4D implemented, manual pending: production prefab and per-world service integration. Later complete suites include 258/258 Edit Mode and 18/18 Play Mode, but the dedicated manual checklist remains open.

items.title: 9 October 2026 and earlier
items.text:
• Two-layer world data, classification, Tilemap projection, collision, and whole-body clearance progressed through accepted milestones 2.1B–2.2B.
  • 2.2C capability automation passed 37/37 focused, 192/192 complete Edit Mode, 2/2 movement regressions, and scene validation; its dedicated manual Scene-view checklist remains pending.
  • Bounded autonomous ground, grip, and gravity milestones established the reusable movement states later realigned by 2.4A.
  • The original surface-movement prototype established a regression baseline, but its complete milestone acceptance remains unfinished.

For exact checklists, blockers, benchmark context, and retained limitations, consult Documentation/CurrentGameState.md.

items.title: Project shape
items.text:
• Unity 6000.3.8f1
  • 2D Universal Render Pipeline
  • New Input System
  • C# runtime code under Assets/AntColony/Scripts/
  • Edit Mode and Play Mode tests under Assets/AntColony/Tests/
  • Authored scenes and prefabs under Assets/AntColony/
  • No networking package; the game is single-player

The project preserves an authored-content-first approach. Scene and prefab references remain explicit, while plain-C# models own game state where Unity components are unnecessary.

items.title: Runtime ownership
items.text:
flowchart TB
  subgraph Data[Plain C# authoritative data]
    AR[AntRecord and AntRegistry]
    WD[ChunkedWorldData]
    SI[SurvivalInteractionWorld]
  end

  subgraph Rules[Rules and shared services]
    CAP[Clearance and movement capability]
    MAP[GridNavigationMap]
    SCH[GridNavigationScheduler]
    GWS[GridNavigationWorldService]
  end

  subgraph Unity[Unity-facing components]
    BIND[AntEntityBinding]
    CTRL[AntSelectionCommandController]
    MOTOR[GridNavigationMotor]
    TILE[Tilemap renderers]
    HOST[AntGameDevelopmentWorldHost]
  end

  WD --> CAP --> MAP --> SCH --> GWS --> MOTOR
  WD --> TILE
  AR --> BIND --> CTRL
  CTRL --> MOTOR
  SI --> CTRL
  HOST --> Data
  HOST --> Rules
  HOST --> Unity

items.title: Ant data
items.text: AntColony.Ants owns stable identity, colony membership, caste, attributes, lifecycle, skills, and needs. Runtime visuals bind to records rather than becoming the source of truth.

items.title: World data
items.text: AntColony.World owns chunks, Background/Solid material definitions, classification, clearance, capability, pathfinding data, and scheduling. Visual and collision Tilemaps project that data through AntColony.WorldPresentation.

items.title: Navigation
items.text: One GridNavigationWorldService owns the shared navigation map and bounded scheduler for a world. Each GridNavigationMotor owns only its agent request and execution state. Command and interaction systems call the narrow motor API.

items.title: Commands and interactions
items.text: AntColony.Commands handles selection, context orders, visual bindings, and the narrow physical-survival interaction slice. Location-owned storage and reservations live in the plain-C# SurvivalInteractionWorld, not in UI labels or Tilemap visuals.

items.title: Development composition
items.text: AntGameDevelopmentWorldHost assembles the deterministic integrated test world. It is a focused authored coordinator, not a global production manager. Developer controls and diagnostics expose authoritative state for acceptance checks.

items.title: Scene flow
items.text:
Scene Purpose Status AntMovementPrototype.unity Continuous-input surface movement regression course Retained developer fixture AntNavigationPrototype.unity Navigation classification and visualisation fixture Retained developer fixture AntGameDevelopment.unity Integrated world, ants, selection, grid movement, needs, and interactions Primary development scene

There is no finished menu-to-game flow, Bootstrap scene, save selection, or production world-loading sequence yet. Future work must preserve the existing authored coordinator seams rather than introducing an unnecessary global manager.

items.title: Test strategy
items.text:
• Plain-C# Edit Mode tests cover deterministic records, world rules, pathfinding, scheduling, and interactions.
  • Physics-backed tests cover collider projection, movement, falling, and integration behavior.
  • Play Mode tests cover scene wiring and end-to-end interaction slices.
  • Structural validators inspect authored scenes and prefabs.
  • Manual checklists cover visuals, input, timing, diagnostics, and behaviors that automation does not observe.

Compilation, automated tests, and manual acceptance are recorded separately. A successful build never implies Unity Play Mode acceptance.

items.title: Architectural guardrails
items.text:
• Keep input/commands, task choice, navigation, motor execution, physics, and presentation separate.
  • Preserve Unity .meta files and serialized references.
  • Use Unity-aware null checks (component == null) for destroyed objects.
  • Prefer local invalidation and shared maps over per-ant world duplication.
  • Add major dependencies only after an identified need and explicit approval.

See the Documentation Workflow for keeping this page synchronized.
